name: Gbenga-Adeyemi Stephanie
missingPieces: D1 omits two real findings: the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (A05/CWE-798) and the cookie missing Secure/SameSite flags (A05/CWE-614). D2 chain skips the recon 02:14:08 and failed-guess 02:14:55 hops and does not weave stored XSS and open redirect into the ordered chain. SQLi CVSS uses A:H instead of A:N.
feedback: On D1 you catalogued eight of the ten planted findings with the right OWASP class, a correct or defensible CWE, and a quoted source line or capture timestamp for almost all of them, which is genuinely strong work. SQL injection at lines 64-67 reconciled to 02:15:31 admin' OR '1'='1 returning 302, the alg:none token forgery proven with Token 2, MD5 hashing (CWE-327 is an acceptable variant of the intended CWE-916), no-expiry, stored XSS at 02:18:47 with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, XXE, path traversal at 02:24:02, and open redirect at 02:21:13 are all proved at the mechanism level. You also nailed the decoy: you named the hand-rolled verify loop as the tempting construct and disproved it by showing hash_equals is constant-time, and you did not fall into mislabelling alg:none as the safe one. What costs you in D1 is two missing findings, the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (A05 or A02, CWE-798) and the cookie lacking Secure and SameSite (A05, CWE-614); the secret in particular is a substantial finding, so this is not a near-perfect catalogue. On D2 your PoC payloads per hop are verbatim and correct, and your impact section is the right shape: 312 customers, the 20-row sample summing to about four million naira, and a stated-assumption projection to roughly sixty-three million, anchored to the BoltCash launch in six weeks. Two things hold D2 back: the chain is compressed into four paths that omit the recon (02:14:08) and failed-guess (02:14:55) hops and do not place stored XSS and open redirect into the ordered narrative, and your SQLi CVSS vector uses A:H to reach 9.8 when the authentication bypass does not affect availability, so the correct vector is CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. D3 is your strongest deliverable: the executive summary ends on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model names the shared /api/v1/internal trust as the scope-changing pivot, findings are tied to evidence lines, the decoy is restated correctly, and crucially your remediation is ordered by risk-reduction-per-hour and not by CVSS, with the two-hour WAF block first, the one-to-two-day token fix second, and the multi-week prepared-statement rewrite last; your two detection stopgaps both give an exact field and a false-positive estimate. Watch one slip in D3: you call the platform Django when the code is PHP. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice at about 380 words, cites ISC2 Canon II by number, and ties NDPA 2023 Section 40 and the 72-hour NDPC duty to the PII loss; to make it complete you should have also cited Section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects given the high risk to them. Nothing here is fabricated, every figure traces to the exfil sample with assumptions shown, so there is no penalty. The single most important fix is to stop dropping findings and complete the catalogue: add the hardcoded JWT secret and the cookie-flags finding, because a clean ten-of-ten with correct CVSS availability scoring is what separates this from a top mark.
